Each entry is told to the AI game master (src/director.js prompt: hero.standing, party[].standing) and shown in the Journal when its `when` holds, checked like a written line's when (src/expansion.js lineApplies). Facts only: what was chosen, never what to do with it.

entries.text: The hero's Second Oath answers to the council of the free wards, which can recall them by two-thirds.
The hero's Second Oath answers to Briarwatch, the town that took them in.
The hero's Second Oath answers to the people they walk with: their companions.
The hero's Second Oath answers to no one: to what is right, as best they can see it.
Nessa wrote Wren a long yes: she will take Cinder Fold's forge-signal after her, but not yet.
Nessa is keeper of Cinder Fold's forge-signal. Wren gave her the key at the pit before she was cast into the tenth bell.
Nessa turned her long yes into a real one: she went back over the pass in the spring to take the forge-signal from Wren.
Nessa's yes to Wren's post is held for her. Wren keeps the forge-signal from a chair, alive and still angry about it.
Nessa turned down Wren's forge-signal post in a letter she sealed herself, and chose the road with the hero. Wren kept the no and will not ask again.
Wren was cast into Cinder Fold's tenth bell. The miners' committee holds the signal key Nessa said no to.
Nessa never answered Wren's offer of the forge-signal. The letter is still in her pocket.
